items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: they may have felt that they owned the name as they owned Baron Lee.

ctx.x: The name ... you had given permission for the name to be used, or did it sort of refer to you?

Well, that's a very strange thing, because at this moment, I can't recall -- maybe they may have even felt ... when I say 'they' I mean the Mills organization, -- they may have felt that they owned the name as they owned Baron Lee. Duke Ellington was, of course, Duke Ellington's name, Earl Hines was his name -- so they wouldn't have owned that. But King Carter was not necessarily my name, nor was it a name that I went by as a nickname at that time.
And they recorded -- that the King Carter group recorded "Blues in My Heart".
